course_name_original: Mantenimiento y Fiabilidad de Máquinas e Instalaciones Eléctricas
course_name_en: Maintenance and Reliability of Electrical Machines and Installations
prerequisites: Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of general electromagnetism laws and their application.
Understanding and mastery of constructive and functional aspects of electrical machines and installations.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the appropriate testing technique for the maintenance of each electrical equipment and to characterize each specific type of fault.
Select the correct electronic instrumentation for a given test.
Correctly handle, with appropriate risk prevention, the instrumentation necessary to perform a test.
Describe and differentiate classical and advanced techniques regarding testing procedures, sensors, instrumentation, and criteria used for detecting anomalies in electrical equipment.
Differentiate magnitudes and parameters that allow identifying the existence of anomalies or faults in electrical equipment.

syllabus_topics: Constructive aspects of power transformers: magnetic materials, conductor insulation, and operations with oil.
Constructive aspects of the induction motor: rotor manufacturing technology, sheet types, low and medium voltage motors, mica-epoxy insulators.
Constructive aspects of the synchronous machine: properties of the machine as a generator. Real operator manual of an electrical plant.
Signal analysis in the frequency domain: fundamentals of spectral analysis.
Instrumentation and analysis techniques. Vibration analysis, accelerometers. Current analysis: types of probes.
Diagnosis based on spectral analysis of the supply current.
Visit to industrial facilities of an electrical sector company (electrical machine manufacturer).
Practice 1: Signal analysis in the frequency domain.
Practice 2: Detection of rotor asymmetries in induction motors using current analysis.
Practice 3: Diagnosis of mechanical faults using vibration analysis.
Practice 4: Diagnosis of main insulation using off-line tests.
Practice 5: Applications of impulse tests. Partial discharge tests.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (use of real test equipment, report writing)
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 50% from two partial written theory exams and 50% from laboratory practices. Each partial exam and each laboratory practice session are evaluated. For the extraordinary examination or differentiated evaluation, an exam covering the entire subject, including questions related to test equipment and setups, will be conducted, as it is not possible to repeat the practices.
